## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 51 (titled *Surusurukāraka* and translated as "Slurping") is a training rule for Buddhist monks preserved in the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule belongs to the sekhiya division of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*, which outlines monastic etiquette and proper deportment, specifically forbidding monks from making a slurping sound while eating [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule and its accompanying case material has been made by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

The rule against slurping has extensive parallels across all known early Buddhist Vinaya traditions [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali Vinaya, exact counterparts are preserved in the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (Sekhiya 51), the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Pātimokkha (Sekhiya 51), and the Parivāra [SuttaCentral]. Cross-tradition parallels are widely attested across Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan canonical vinayas, including the recensions of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, and Lokottaravāda schools [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also registers close structural parallels with Sekhiya 50 (*Capucapukāraka*, prohibiting smacking noises while eating) across multiple school traditions [SuttaCentral].

Textual reuse analysis by DharmaNexus records 238 matching passages shared between Sekhiya 51 and 71 other Pali texts, reflecting the standard introductory and procedural formulaic phrasing found across the Vinaya [DharmaNexus]. The largest Pali reuse partners include several Khandhaka chapters—such as the Mahākhandhaka (Kd 1), Cīvarakkhandhaka (Kd 8), and Senāsanakkhandhaka (Kd 16)—as well as various Pācittiya rules (such as Pc 12 and Pc 46) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignment, DharmaNexus identifies a match with a Tibetan Vinaya text in the Kangyur (BO_K01_D0003-2_H0003-2) [DharmaNexus]. No secondary literature passages in the dossier discuss this Vinaya text directly.
